"'''Stay'''" (stylized in [[all caps]]) is a song by Australian rapper and singer [[the Kid Laroi]] and Canadian singer [[Justin Bieber]]. It was released through Grade A Productions and [[Columbia Records]] on 9 July 2021, as the lead single (sixth overall) from Laroi's reloaded mixtape, ''[[F*ck Love|F*ck Love 3: Over You]]''. Laroi and Bieber wrote the song with Haan, [[FnZ]] members Finatik & Zac, and producers [[Cashmere Cat]], [[Charlie Puth]], [[Omer Fedi]], and [[Blake Slatkin]]. The song marks the second collaboration between the two artists, following Bieber's song, "[[Unstable (song)|Unstable]]", a track from his sixth studio album, ''[[Justice (Justin Bieber album)|Justice]]'' (2021).

"Stay" reached number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming Laroi's first chart-topping single and Bieber's eighth, and additionally topped the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]]. Furthermore, it reached number one in 21 other countries, including their respective natives Australia and  Canada, along with Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, South Korea, and Sweden. It also peaked within the top ten in 18 other countries. At the [[2021 ARIA Music Awards]], the song won the [[ARIA Award for Best Pop Release]], which resulted in Laroi and Bieber both winning the [[ARIA Award for Best Artist]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://themusicnetwork.com/2021-aria-awards-nominees/ |title=ARIA Awards nominees revealed: Amy Shark & Genesis Owusu lead the charge |work=[[The Music Network]] |date=20 October 2021 |access-date=24 October 2021 |author=Kelly, Vivienne |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020000045/https://themusicnetwork.com/2021-aria-awards-nominees/ |archive-date=20 October 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> At the [[APRA Music Awards of 2022]], the song won the award for Song of the Year.<ref name="APRA2022Noms">{{cite web|url=https://theindustryobserver.thebrag.com/nominees-revealed-for-2022-apra-music-awards/|title=Nominees Revealed for 2022 APRA Music Awards|website=The Industry Observer|date=7 April 2022|access-date=9 April 2022|archive-date=31 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531230042/https://theindustryobserver.thebrag.com/nominees-revealed-for-2022-apra-music-awards/|url-status=live}}</ref>

"Stay" (stylized in all caps) is a song by Australian rapper and singer the Kid Laroi and Canadian singer Justin Bieber. It was released through Grade A Productions and Columbia Records on 9 July 2021, as the lead single (sixth overall) from Laroi's reloaded mixtape, F*ck Love 3: Over You. Laroi and Bieber wrote the song with Haan, FnZ members Finatik & Zac, and producers Cashmere Cat, Charlie Puth, Omer Fedi, and Blake Slatkin. The song marks the second collaboration between the two artists, following Bieber's song, "Unstable", a track from his sixth studio album, Justice (2021).

"Stay" reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming Laroi's first chart-topping single and Bieber's eighth, and additionally topped the Billboard Global 200. Furthermore, it reached number one in 21 other countries, including their respective natives Australia and  Canada, along with Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, South Korea, and Sweden. It also peaked within the top ten in 18 other countries. At the 2021 ARIA Music Awards, the song won the ARIA Award for Best Pop Release, which resulted in Laroi and Bieber both winning the ARIA Award for Best Artist. At the APRA Music Awards of 2022, the song won the award for Song of the Year.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
On 20 September 2020, Laroi shared a snippet of the song on an [[Instagram]] live stream, followed by a longer snippet in better quality that was previewed on a live stream from Rolling Loud on 29 October 2020. Bieber's contribution to the song was revealed on 31 May 2021. The song leaked in full on a [[Discord (software)|Discord]] server on 2 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=New The Kid LAROI & Justin Bieber Song 'Stay' Surfaces Online|url=https://hiphop-n-more.com/2021/06/new-the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-song-stay-surfaces-online/|website=HipHopNMore|author=HHNM Staff|date=2 June 2021|access-date=1 July 2021|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709182738/https://hiphop-n-more.com/2021/06/new-the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-song-stay-surfaces-online/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref>

"Stay" marks Laroi's first major single release as a lead artist in 2021 and Bieber's first major single as a lead artist since the release of his second extended play, ''[[Freedom (EP)|Freedom]]'', which was released in April 2021. On 3 June 2021, [[Scooter Braun]], who has been Bieber's manager from the start of his career, also became Laroi's manager, until Laroi left and joined [[Adam Leber]] at Rebel Management on 27 September 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Kid LAROI joins Scooter Braun Projects' management roster|url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/the-kid-laroi-joins-scooter-braun-projects-management-roster-2956308|last=Brereton|first=Greta|date=4 June 2021|website=[[NME]]|access-date=1 July 2021|archive-date=23 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210623223800/https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/the-kid-laroi-joins-scooter-braun-projects-management-roster-2956308|url-status=live}}</ref>

Laroi had the song for about a year before its release. He created the song while spending time with producers [[Charlie Puth]], [[Omer Fedi]], and [[Blake Slatkin]] at Slatkin's house. Puth played the melody of the song on the keyboard, but Laroi ended up liking it and wanted to get it in production software [[Pro Tools]] to use it to create a song. He felt that "it was probably the most organic way of making a song I've ever done – ever". Laroi thought Bieber "would sound perfect", so he went to the studio at which Bieber records; they finished recording the song, but Bieber was hesitant about whether his vocals sounded good or not.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Kid LAROI talks new single 'Stay' with Justin Bieber and shares update on debut album|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-stay-lyrics-meaning-interview-machine-gun-kelly-debut-album-radar-2987517|last=Lavin|first=Will|date=9 July 2021|website=NME|access-date=9 July 2021|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709062027/https://www.nme.com/news/music/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-stay-lyrics-meaning-interview-machine-gun-kelly-debut-album-radar-2987517|url-status=live}}</ref>

Caramanica found "Stay" to be {{nowrap|"[b]racingly}} effective", considering it a more effective pairing of Laroi and Bieber than their previous collaboration on "Unstable" from the latter's sixth studio album, Justice. Tyler Jenke from Rolling Stone Australia wrote that "the slick new tune" is "undoubtedly one that lives up [to] the hype". Jordan Rose of Complex believed that the track has Laroi and Bieber "leaning into their strengths". Alex Zidel from HotNewHipHop felt that the song is "every bit as infectious as [one] would expect" and thought of it to be "a solid pop offering for the summer". Jason Lipshutz of Billboard opined that the song "sounds like it should push [Laroi] to a new level" of stardom. Uproxx contributing writer Carolyn Droke stated that the "buoyant track['s]" combination of "a euphoric chorus and a driving beat" will make it "the next song of the summer". Rowat commended Laroi and Bieber's partnership as "one of the year's best surprises" and said that the song "capitalizes on both singers' skills as falsettists". DeVille described the song as "maniacally catchy" and thought it musically feels like Laroi "blasting off into a new frontier of crossover success". Curto called the track "a high-energy, synth-filled pop banger". However, he later criticised the song for being "some of Laroi's most anonymous work yet" and concluded that "it could just as easily be a hit for the Weeknd or Post Malone".

"Stay" debuted at number one on the [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Singles Chart]] for the week of 19 July 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/singles-chart/2021-07-19|title=ARIA Top 50 Singles Chart|publisher=[[Australian Recording Industry Association]]|date=19 July 2021|access-date=16 July 2021|archive-date=16 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716070234/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/singles-chart/2021-07-19|url-status=live}}</ref> It became Laroi's second number-one single in Australia after "[[Without You (The Kid Laroi song)|Without You]]" topped the chart for a week in May and Bieber's fifth as a lead artist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-scores-second-aria-1-single-with-justin-bieber-collab-stay|title=The Kid Laroi scores second ARIA #1 single with Justin Bieber collab Stay|date=16 July 2021|publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association|access-date=16 July 2021|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718233259/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-scores-second-aria-1-single-with-justin-bieber-collab-stay|url-status=live}}</ref> It held on to its position for 14 consecutive weeks, [[List of number-one singles of 2021 (Australia)|becoming the longest-running number-one single of 2021]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-and-justin-bieber-stay-at-1-on-aria-singles-chart-for-eighth-week|title=The Kid Laroi and Justin Bieber stay at #1 on ARIA Singles Chart for eighth week|date=3 September 2021|publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association|access-date=3 September 2021|archive-date=3 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903082005/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-and-justin-bieber-stay-at-1-on-aria-singles-chart-for-eighth-week|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-and-justin-bieber-make-it-14-weeks-at-1-on-the-aria-singles-chart|title=The Kid Laroi and Justin Bieber make it 14 weeks at #1 on the ARIA Singles Chart|date=15 October 2021|publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association|access-date=15 October 2021|archive-date=15 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211015060844/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-and-justin-bieber-make-it-14-weeks-at-1-on-the-aria-singles-chart|url-status=live}}</ref> In January 2022, the song returned to the number one spot following the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 2021|2021 Triple J Hottest 100]]'s announcement and remained there for three additional weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-return-to-claim-15th-week-at-aria-singles-chart-1|title=The Kid Laroi & Justin Bieber return to claim 15th week at ARIA Singles Chart #1|date=28 January 2022|publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association|access-date=28 January 2022|archive-date=28 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128060620/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-return-to-claim-15th-week-at-aria-singles-chart-1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-hit-landmark-16-weeks-at-aria-singles-chart-1-with-stay|title=The Kid Laroi & Justin Bieber hit landmark 16 weeks at ARIA Singles Chart #1 with Stay|date=4 February 2022|publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association|access-date=4 February 2022|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205045232/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-hit-landmark-16-weeks-at-aria-singles-chart-1-with-stay|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARIA17">{{cite web|url=https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-make-it-17-weeks-at-aria-singles-chart-1-with-stay|title=The Kid Laroi & Justin Bieber make it 17 weeks at ARIA Singles Chart #1 with Stay|date=11 February 2022|publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association|access-date=11 February 2022|archive-date=11 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211061226/https://www.aria.com.au/charts/news/the-kid-laroi-justin-bieber-make-it-17-weeks-at-aria-singles-chart-1-with-stay|url-status=live}}</ref> Its 17-week reign became the longest run at the top of the ARIA Singles Chart by a male artist(s) and the second-longest overall.<ref name="ARIA17"/>

In New Zealand, "Stay" entered at the top of the [[Official New Zealand Music Chart|New Zealand Singles Chart]], securing Laroi's first number-one single in the country and Bieber's 11th overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nztop40.co.nz/chart/index?chart=5168|title=The Official NZ Music Charts|date=19 July 2021|publisher=[[Recorded Music NZ]]|access-date=2 October 2021|archive-date=2 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211002173139/https://nztop40.co.nz/chart/index?chart=5168|url-status=dead}}</ref> The song spent more weeks at number one than any other by an Australian male, maintaining that position for 11 non-consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nztop40.co.nz/|title=The Official NZ Music Charts|date=30 August 2021|publisher=Recorded Music NZ|access-date=3 September 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210903020240/https://nztop40.co.nz/|archive-date=3 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://nztop40.co.nz/|title=The Official NZ Music Charts|date=4 October 2021|publisher=Recorded Music NZ|access-date=2 October 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211002172102/https://nztop40.co.nz/|archive-date=2 October 2021}}</ref>

In the United Kingdom, "Stay" entered at number five on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on 16 July 2021 – for the week ending dated 22 July 2021 – making it Laroi's second top ten hit in Britain and Bieber's 27th.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheerans-bad-habits-claims-third-week-at-number-1-on-official-singles-chart__33605/|title=Ed Sheeran's Bad Habits claims third week at Number 1 on Official Singles Chart|last=Griffiths|first=George|date=16 July 2021|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=16 July 2021|archive-date=21 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210721050927/https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheerans-bad-habits-claims-third-week-at-number-1-on-official-singles-chart__33605/|url-status=live}}</ref> It rose three places to number two a week later, behind [[Ed Sheeran]]'s "[[Bad Habits (Ed Sheeran song)|Bad Habits]]" during its fourth week at the summit. It stayed at number two for six weeks and became Laroi's joint-highest-charting song in the UK along with "Without You".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheeran-s-bad-habits-scores-another-huge-week-at-number-1-on-the-official-singles-chart__33650/|title=Ed Sheeran's Bad Habits scores another huge week at Number 1 on the Official Singles Chart|last=Ainsley|first=Helen|date=23 July 2021|publisher=Official Charts Company|access-date=23 July 2021|archive-date=23 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723211740/https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheeran-s-bad-habits-scores-another-huge-week-at-number-1-on-the-official-singles-chart__33650/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In Ireland, "Stay" entered at number three on the [[Irish Singles Chart]] as the week's highest new entry. The track became Bieber's 60th top 50 single in the Irish Republic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheerans-bad-habits-claims-third-week-at-number-1-on-official-irish-singles-chart__33599/|title=Ed Sheeran's Bad Habits claims third week at Number 1 on Official Irish Singles Chart|last=White|first=Jack|date=16 July 2021|publisher=Official Charts Company|access-date=16 July 2021|archive-date=16 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716170828/https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheerans-bad-habits-claims-third-week-at-number-1-on-official-irish-singles-chart__33599/|url-status=live}}</ref> The song moved up a spot the following week to a new peak of number two behind "Bad Habits" for eight weeks, becoming Laroi's highest-charting song in Ireland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheeran-makes-it-a-month-at-number-1-on-the-official-irish-singles-chart-with-bad-habits__33645/|title=Ed Sheeran makes it a month at Number 1 on the Official Irish Singles Chart with Bad Habits|last=White|first=Jack|date=23 July 2021|publisher=Official Charts Company|access-date=23 July 2021|archive-date=23 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723150222/https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/ed-sheeran-makes-it-a-month-at-number-1-on-the-official-irish-singles-chart-with-bad-habits__33645/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the United States, "Stay" debuted at number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], starting with 34.7 million streams, 12.9 million in radio audience, and 12,000 in sales.<ref name="BH100">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9603058/bts-permission-to-dance-number-one-hot-100/|title=BTS Blasts Onto Hot 100 at No. 1 With 'Permission to Dance,' The Kid LAROI & Justin Bieber Bow at No. 3 With 'Stay'|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=19 July 2021|magazine=Billboard|access-date=19 July 2021|archive-date=19 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719170556/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9603058/bts-permission-to-dance-number-one-hot-100/|url-status=live}}</ref> It entered atop the [[Streaming Songs]] chart, becoming Laroi's first and Bieber's sixth leader there, and at number five on the [[Digital Songs|Digital Song Sales]] chart.<ref name="BH100"/> Laroi earned his third top 10 hit on the Hot 100 and a new career best, surpassing the number eight peak of "Without You" with [[Miley Cyrus]].<ref name="BH100"/> In addition to Bieber getting his 24th top 10 hit on the chart, he became the youngest artist to have 100 entries appear on the Hot 100 at 27 years and four months old.<ref name="BH100"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://uproxx.com/pop/justin-bieber-youngest-chart-milestone-hot-100/|title=Justin Bieber Is Now The Youngest Artist To Reach A Major Chart Milestone, Beating Drake|last=Rossignol|first=Derrick|date=20 July 2021|website=Uproxx|access-date=21 July 2021|archive-date=23 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723060538/https://uproxx.com/pop/justin-bieber-youngest-chart-milestone-hot-100/|url-status=live}}</ref> On the week of 14 August 2021, the song topped the ''Billboard'' Hot 100, dethroning [[BTS]]' "[[Butter (song)|Butter]]" and becoming Laroi's first and Bieber's eighth number-one hit on the chart.<ref name="bbhot100">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9612247/kid-laroi-justin-bieber-stay-number-one-hot-100/|title=The Kid Laroi & Justin Bieber's 'Stay' Hits No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100|last=Trust|first=Gary|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=9 August 2021|access-date=9 August 2021|archive-date=9 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210809173427/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9612247/kid-laroi-justin-bieber-stay-number-one-hot-100|url-status=live}}</ref> It stayed at the number-one position for four consecutive weeks, surpassing "[[Sorry (Justin Bieber song)|Sorry]]" as Bieber's longest reign as a lead artist.<ref name="bbpopairplay">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9622050/hot-100-story-9-4-21/|title=Extended 'Stay': The Kid LAROI & Justin Bieber Top Billboard Hot 100 For Fourth Week|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=30 August 2021|magazine=Billboard|access-date=30 August 2021|archive-date=30 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830175926/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9622050/hot-100-story-9-4-21/|url-status=live}}</ref> The song also became Laroi's first number one on the [[Mainstream Top 40|Pop Airplay]] chart (where it went on to spend 13 weeks at #1, the second longest run at #1 in the history of the chart, behind [[Ace of Base]]'s "[[The Sign (song)|The Sign]]"), while Bieber tied [[Bruno Mars]] for the most number ones on the chart among solo males with nine each.<ref name="bbpopairplay"/> On the week of 25 September 2021, "Stay" returned to number one on the Hot 100 for a fifth week as it topped the [[Radio Songs (chart)|Radio Songs]] chart for the first time, becoming the first and fifth leader for Laroi and Bieber, respectively.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9632692/kid-laroi-stay-number-one-fifth-week-hot-100/|title=The Kid LAROI & Justin Bieber's 'Stay' Returns to No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=20 September 2021|magazine=Billboard|access-date=20 September 2021|archive-date=20 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920180810/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9632692/kid-laroi-stay-number-one-fifth-week-hot-100/|url-status=live}}</ref> The song spent seven non-consecutive weeks at number one on the Hot 100.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9643530/kid-laroi-justin-bieber-stay-tops-hot-100-wizkid-essence-top-10|title=The Kid LAROI & Justin Bieber's 'Stay' Rules Billboard Hot 100, Wizkid's 'Essence' Hits Top 10|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=11 October 2021|magazine=Billboard|access-date=11 October 2021|archive-date=11 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011225104/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/9643530/kid-laroi-justin-bieber-stay-tops-hot-100-wizkid-essence-top-10/|url-status=live}}</ref> It additionally logged  14 non-consecutive weeks at number two of the Hot 100.<ref name="STAY14WEEKS">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/glass-animals-heat-waves-latto-big-energy-hot-100-1235055058/|title=Glass Animals' 'Heat Waves' Rules Hot 100 For Fifth Week, Latto's 'Big Energy' Leaps to No. 3|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=4 April 2022|access-date=4 April 2022|archive-date=4 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404225349/https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/glass-animals-heat-waves-latto-big-energy-hot-100-1235055058/|url-status=live}}</ref> As of the chart dated 2 April 2022, "Stay" also broke the records for the most weeks spent in the Hot 100's top two and top three spots, with 21 and 23 weeks respectively.<ref name="STAY14WEEKS" /> The record has since been surpassed by [[Harry Styles]]' "[[As It Was]]" with 25 and 29 weeks, respectively in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cowen |first=Trace William |date=27 September 2022 |title=Harry Styles' "As It Was" Becomes Longest-Running Solo No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100 Chart |url=https://www.complex.com/music/harry-styles-as-it-was-longest-running-solo-number-one-billboard-hot-100 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208033150/https://www.complex.com/music/harry-styles-as-it-was-longest-running-solo-number-one-billboard-hot-100 |archive-date=8 December 2022 |access-date=2022-11-13 |website=Complex |language=en}}</ref> On 18 April 2022, "Stay" became the first song in history to spend its first 40 weeks consecutively in the top 10 of the Hot 100.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/jack-harlow-first-class-number-one-debut-billboard-hot-100-1235060319/|title=Jack Harlow Flies 'First Class' to No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=18 April 2022|access-date=18 April 2022|archive-date=18 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418194955/https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/jack-harlow-first-class-number-one-debut-billboard-hot-100-1235060319/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 June 2023, the song was certified diamond by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA).<ref name="RIAA"/>

On the [[Rolling Stone Top 100|''Rolling Stone'' Top 100]], the song earned Laroi his first number one with 30.8 million streams on opening week.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/rs-charts-top-100-the-kid-laroi-stay-1198943/|title=RS Charts: The Kid Laroi Earns First Number One With 'Stay'|last=Leight|first=Elias|date=19 July 2021|magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=22 July 2021|archive-date=22 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210722055011/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/rs-charts-top-100-the-kid-laroi-stay-1198943/|url-status=live}}</ref> It spent seven straight weeks at number one on the chart, becoming just the third song to do so after [[Roddy Ricch]]'s "[[The Box (Roddy Ricch song)|The Box]]" and Rodrigo's "Good 4 U".<ref>{{cite sections.text:
"Stay" debuted at number one on the ARIA Singles Chart for the week of 19 July 2021. It became Laroi's second number-one single in Australia after "Without You" topped the chart for a week in May and Bieber's fifth as a lead artist. It held on to its position for 14 consecutive weeks, becoming the longest-running number-one single of 2021. In January 2022, the song returned to the number one spot following the 2021 Triple J Hottest 100's announcement and remained there for three additional weeks. Its 17-week reign became the longest run at the top of the ARIA Singles Chart by a male artist(s) and the second-longest overall.

In New Zealand, "Stay" entered at the top of the New Zealand Singles Chart, securing Laroi's first number-one single in the country and Bieber's 11th overall. The song spent more weeks at number one than any other by an Australian male, maintaining that position for 11 non-consecutive weeks.

In the United Kingdom, "Stay" entered at number five on the UK Singles Chart on 16 July 2021 – for the week ending dated 22 July 2021 – making it Laroi's second top ten hit in Britain and Bieber's 27th. It rose three places to number two a week later, behind Ed Sheeran's "Bad Habits" during its fourth week at the summit. It stayed at number two for six weeks and became Laroi's joint-highest-charting song in the UK along with "Without You".

In Ireland, "Stay" entered at number three on the Irish Singles Chart as the week's highest new entry. The track became Bieber's 60th top 50 single in the Irish Republic. The song moved up a spot the following week to a new peak of number two behind "Bad Habits" for eight weeks, becoming Laroi's highest-charting song in Ireland.

In the United States, "Stay" debuted at number three on the Billboard Hot 100, starting with 34.7 million streams, 12.9 million in radio audience, and 12,000 in sales. It entered atop the Streaming Songs chart, becoming Laroi's first and Bieber's sixth leader there, and at number five on the Digital Song Sales chart. Laroi earned his third top 10 hit on the Hot 100 and a new career best, surpassing the number eight peak of "Without You" with Miley Cyrus. In addition to Bieber getting his 24th top 10 hit on the chart, he became the youngest artist to have 100 entries appear on the Hot 100 at 27 years and four months old. On the week of 14 August 2021, the song topped the Billboard Hot 100, dethroning BTS' "Butter" and becoming Laroi's first and Bieber's eighth number-one hit on the chart. It stayed at the number-one position for four consecutive weeks, surpassing "Sorry" as Bieber's longest reign as a lead artist. The song also became Laroi's first number one on the Pop Airplay chart (where it went on to spend 13 weeks at #1, the second longest run at #1 in the history of the chart, behind Ace of Base's "The Sign"), while Bieber tied Bruno Mars for the most number ones on the chart among solo males with nine each. On the week of 25 September 2021, "Stay" returned to number one on the Hot 100 for a fifth week as it topped the Radio Songs chart for the first time, becoming the first and fifth leader for Laroi and Bieber, respectively. The song spent seven non-consecutive weeks at number one on the Hot 100. It additionally logged  14 non-consecutive weeks at number two of the Hot 100. As of the chart dated 2 April 2022, "Stay" also broke the records for the most weeks spent in the Hot 100's top two and top three spots, with 21 and 23 weeks respectively. The record has since been surpassed by Harry Styles' "As It Was" with 25 and 29 weeks, respectively in 2022. On 18 April 2022, "Stay" became the first song in history to spend its first 40 weeks consecutively in the top 10 of the Hot 100. On 23 June 2023, the song was certified diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).

On the Rolling Stone Top 100, the song earned Laroi his first number one with 30.8 million streams on opening week. It spent seven straight weeks at number one on the chart, becoming just the third song to do so after Roddy Ricch's "The Box" and Rodrigo's "Good 4 U". The track was named "2021's Song of the Summer" by Variety based on a song project report from Alpha Data, where it earned 1.5 million units. As of 28 October 2021, the song has accumulated 1.1 billion in airplay audience and 537.6 million U.S. streams and has sold 177,200 downloads.

"Stay" additionally topped the charts in Austria, both regions of Belgium (Flanders and Wallonia), Bieber's native Canada, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Iceland, India, Israel, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Norway, Singapore, Slovakia, South Korea, and Sweden, and peaked within the top 10 in France, Italy, the Japan Hot 100, Portugal, and Switzerland. Worldwide, the song debuted at number two on the Billboard Global 200 behind BTS's "Permission to Dance". It opened with 76.3 million streams and 18,600 sold. The song ascended to number one on its third week with 75.1 million streams and 13,900 in sales, making it Laroi's first leader on the chart and Bieber's second after "Peaches". It later topped the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. on the chart dated 21 August 2021, dethroning "Bad Habits". The song was the longest-reigning number one on the Global 200, at the time and the first to lead it for double-digits, spending a total of eleven weeks at the top of the chart. On 4 November 2021, the song reportedly reached one billion streams on Spotify, becoming the fastest to do so in 118 days and surpassing the previous record held by Sheeran with "Shape of You" in 153 days. "Stay" was the most-streamed song globally on Apple Music in 2022.
